questions.chapterTitle: Personal Protective Equipment and Respiratory Protection
questions.stem: A facility issues the same gloves and safety glasses to every department without documenting task hazards. Several chemicals permeate the selected gloves. What is the best corrective action?
options: Perform and certify a task-based PPE hazard assessment, select compatible equipment, communicate limitations, and train affected employees
Replace the gloves only after a worker experiences visible skin injury
Keep the standardized PPE because uniformity is more important than chemical compatibility
Ask employees to choose any gloves that feel comfortable without reviewing permeation data
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PPE selection must follow a documented hazard assessment and account for chemical, physical, fit, and task factors; one generic selection cannot be assumed protective.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Replace the gloves only after a worker experiences visible skin injury' does not apply the controlling principle for ppe hazard assessment to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Keep the standardized PPE because uniformity is more important than chemical compatibility' does not apply the controlling principle for ppe hazard assessment to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Ask employees to choose any gloves that feel comfortable without reviewing permeation data' does not apply the controlling principle for ppe hazard assessment to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.chapterTitle: Personal Protective Equipment and Respiratory Protection
questions.stem: A vessel may contain an unknown concentration of a highly toxic gas, and entry cannot be delayed for full characterization. Which respiratory protection approach is most defensible?
options: Select any tight-fitting respirator if the worker passes a qualitative fit test
Treat the atmosphere as potentially IDLH and use an appropriate positive-pressure supplied-air respirator with auxiliary escape or a positive-pressure SCBA
Use an air-purifying respirator with the highest available cartridge
Use a filtering facepiece because the worker will remain inside only a few minutes
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Unknown concentrations and potentially IDLH conditions require atmosphere-supplying protection designed for IDLH entry; air-purifying devices depend on known contaminants and adequate oxygen.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Select any tight-fitting respirator if the worker passes a qualitative fit test' does not apply the controlling principle for respirator selection and idlh to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Use an air-purifying respirator with the highest available cartridge' does not apply the controlling principle for respirator selection and idlh to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Use a filtering facepiece because the worker will remain inside only a few minutes' does not apply the controlling principle for respirator selection and idlh to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.chapterTitle: Personal Protective Equipment and Respiratory Protection
questions.stem: A supervisor wants a new employee to complete a fit test and begin mandatory respirator use before medical review because the project is behind schedule. What should occur?
options: Replace medical evaluation with a signed employee waiver
Allow one shift of use before medical evaluation if the respirator is negative pressure
Complete the required medical evaluation and obtain clearance before fit testing or required respirator use
Fit test first because fit testing determines medical ability to wear a respirator
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Mandatory respirator use can impose physiological burden. Medical evaluation must occur before fit testing or required use, and employees cannot waive that program element.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Replace medical evaluation with a signed employee waiver' does not apply the controlling principle for medical evaluation before respirator use to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Allow one shift of use before medical evaluation if the respirator is negative pressure' does not apply the controlling principle for medical evaluation before respirator use to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Fit test first because fit testing determines medical ability to wear a respirator' does not apply the controlling principle for medical evaluation before respirator use to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: An employee passes a fit test, then loses substantial weight and reports that the facepiece seal feels different. What should the program administrator do?
options: Tighten straps as much as possible and continue work without reassessment
Switch to a different tight-fitting facepiece without any fit test
Wait until the next annual test because early retesting is prohibited
Arrange an additional fit test and reassess facepiece size or model before relying on the respirator

The option 'Wait until the next annual test because early retesting is prohibited' does not apply the controlling principle for fit testing and facepiece changes to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.chapterTitle: Personal Protective Equipment and Respiratory Protection
questions.stem: Employees use organic vapor cartridges for a contaminant with poor warning properties. The program replaces cartridges only when workers smell vapor. What is the main deficiency?
options: The program needs an objective cartridge change schedule or end-of-service-life indicator based on service conditions, not odor detection
Replace cartridges only when breathing resistance increases, without using a change schedule or service-life information
A fit test automatically determines cartridge service life
Odor is the preferred federal method for every organic vapor
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Change schedules must protect before breakthrough. Odor thresholds and individual perception are unreliable and are not a substitute for an objective basis.

The option 'A fit test automatically determines cartridge service life' does not apply the controlling principle for cartridge change schedule to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'Odor is the preferred federal method for every organic vapor' does not apply the controlling principle for cartridge change schedule to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: Air monitoring shows no respirator is required, but employees wish to use elastomeric half-mask respirators voluntarily. What should the employer evaluate?

Ensure use does not create a hazard, provide the required voluntary-use information, and implement applicable medical and maintenance elements
Prohibit all voluntary use because respirators may be used only above an exposure limit
Allow use with no information or evaluation because the employer did not require it

questions.stem: A glove chart lists excellent degradation resistance but a very short permeation breakthrough time for the solvent and task duration. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Good degradation resistance proves the glove prevents permeation for the entire shift
Double-gloving with the same material always doubles breakthrough time exactly
The glove may remain physically intact while the chemical passes through, so a different material or replacement strategy is needed
Breakthrough time matters only when holes are visibly present

The option 'Breakthrough time matters only when holes are visibly present' does not apply the controlling principle for chemical protective clothing breakthrough to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A grinding task presents high-speed particle impact to the eyes and face. Which PPE arrangement is most appropriate?
options: Close one eye while positioning the face shield near the tool
Use ordinary prescription glasses beneath no additional protection
Use a face shield alone because it replaces primary eye protection
Wear suitable safety spectacles or goggles as primary eye protection with a face shield as secondary face protection

The option 'Use ordinary prescription glasses beneath no additional protection' does not apply the controlling principle for eye and face protection layering to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Use a face shield alone because it replaces primary eye protection' does not apply the controlling principle for eye and face protection layering to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: During a supplied-air respirator decision, solve the following problem and select the best answer: A contaminant has an OSHA exposure limit of 2 ppm. options: 200 ppm, because the exposure limit is multiplied by the APF twice for a half-mask respirator.
30 ppm, because the IDLH value always becomes the routine maximum use concentration.
2 ppm, because a respirator cannot be used above the exposure limit.
20 ppm, because APF × exposure limit equals 20 ppm, below the IDLH concentration.
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The calculated MUC is APF × exposure limit = 10 × 2 ppm = 20 ppm. Because 20 ppm is below the stated IDLH value and no lower cartridge limit is given, 20 ppm controls.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The APF is applied once; multiplying it twice overstates the respirator’s protective capability.
The IDLH value is a ceiling on routine MUC calculations, but it does not replace a lower APF-based result.
Respirators may be selected to control exposure above a limit when used within their assigned protection and other program requirements.
